What you see. What we know.

OBSERVATION

Satellite imagery & greenness

Bundled Sentinel-2 background: 9 March 2024. Seasonal NDVI composites: 2022–2025. The monthly card uses a dated clear scene from the selected month. Gaps remain gaps.

ESA Sentinel-2 L2A ↗
TERRAIN ESTIMATE

The shape of the land

Burirhat uses NASADEM HGT v001, approximately 30 m cells, based on February 2000 observations. Small drains and bunds are unresolved. Height exaggeration and interpolation add no measurements.

NASA Earthdata ↗
REGIONAL CONTEXT

Weather has a different scale

NASA POWER monthly values use the uploaded daily archive through October 2026 for the example fields. New fields request their own regional weather for the selected year. These are historical values, not forecasts or field sensors.

NASA POWER ↗
ILLUSTRATION

Crops & soil are a planning view

Crop geometry, density, size, roots, soil colours, soil-layer thicknesses and planting months are illustrative. The soil block is enlarged vertically for inspection and is not a measured underground profile. Sequences are from your existing project. They are not validated recommendations, yield predictions or reconstructed real plants.

USDA: cover, roots & diversity ↗

Why these features help

The isolated 3D field follows the selected polygon and sampled terrain. Switch to Satellite terrain for geographic context; use Soil cutaway to inspect an illustrative underground section. Click the field to inspect an elevation sample. Dated vegetation records reveal seasonal changes. Crop previews make rotation sequences easier to discuss. Local notes provide crop history, water access and soil tests that satellites cannot confirm.

Before making a field decision

Greenness cannot diagnose disease, nutrients or water stress alone. Terrain cannot predict flood depth alone. This demo does not infer NPK values, irrigation doses, suitability rankings or profit. Discuss crop choice and timing with a local agricultural adviser.

Online basemaps & new locations

Esri World Imagery acquisition dates vary and are not reported here. Outside the demo area, Mapzen Terrain Tiles provide mixed-source elevation, not exclusively NASA data. If a service fails, the unavailable data is clearly marked. Crop previews use representative plants; software compatibility rendering omits wind animation. The field model takes visual inspiration from the supplied soil-cutaway demo and GeoPard’s browser-based 3D layer workflow.
